title: Simple, yet Powerful.
body:
I am surprised how much I love this app. I started by doing the usual things. I plugged in the date when I quit smoking and when I went vegan. Very interesting to see how much time elapsed. I love playing with color options and formats… you can view the length of elapsed time in different ways, like days, months, and years. 

I love the reset function as well. If you need to reset you just tap the button and it restarts the count. 

Where I really was surprised is how often I use it. I recently had eye surgery and logged it in. My doctor asked how long it was since my surgery I was able to tell him to the minute lol. We were monitoring how long I had the gas bubble visible in my eye. 

I love this app for everything it does. Seriously. It’s simple, clean, elegant and it works flawlessly. 

Let’s support our Indie developers! Job well done.

title: No more questions on “how long have you been together?”
body:
I was tired. I couldn’t help it any longer. I knew the dates, each one of them. When we met, the year we started dating for real, when did we move in together, the wedding… But I couldn’t keep track of doing the math each time anyone asked “how long have you been together?”
Days Since helped me put an end on this debate. Now I just can open the app and check it out: this many years we’ve known each other, that much years dating, a long time living together, X years of marriage. 
Bonus: I can also track when I started doing something good for myself (such as regular exercise) and how long have I stopped a bad habit. It has been fun, thanks developers for this very easy to use and awesome app.

title: Genuine dev team
body:
First off, the development team seems genuine and true to their word that they are here to help. If you look at other apps on the AppStore a lot of them seem like they want to help but money is definitely a driving factor for them. The fact that this team gives you a week trial and tells you to set a calendar reminder to cancel so you won’t be charged is huge. The app is about $20 a year after the trial which to me I usually wouldn’t consider paying. Due to the genuine attitude this team is portraying I have absolutely no problem paying. They don’t sell your data and what they keep is anonymized according to their privacy policy. The app is simple, looks good, and is straight to the point.

One feature that this app lacks that I would love to see is the ability to edit a note after resetting a timer. I often reset the timer with a note, and reset it again after vaping with a new note on how I feel about what I just did or how my day was going etc. I would like to edit the note so I can do this without impacting the timer.

Other than that missing feature, this app is great and I love the widget. Keep up the work, I and I’m sure many others appreciate what you are doing to help us manage this addiction.

title: Admittedly, I only use this app for a joke

Myself, being an insensitive ~jokester,~ downloaded this app because I needed something to track the days since “they thought it was safe to eat.” My friend is kind of a dunce who doesn’t pay attention to what food they put in their face and, as such, make mistakes when judging the safety of their meals and make themselves sick. This happens every few weeks or so. Hence the day counter. It works well for what it is, and I’m sure that people who need more serious trackers (or light-hearted ones) would find this absolutely acceptable. I do wish that it wouldn’t ask me for the premium version so much, but I understand revenue is revenue and I’m not gonna begrudge you guys for asking for money. I only need the app for a joke so I don’t foresee myself paying, but I don’t think that the free version is in any way lacking. Overall, it works great and my friend and I enjoy the joke.

title: This app is great! Helps you discipline yourself by holding you accountable
body:
Been using it to years to tack my abstinence streak of various things i decided were no good for me (ex: alcohol, soda, red meat/poultry, pornography, vaping). I use it help myself practice temperance/moderation in other areas of my life (ex: eating out, staying up late, using NRT products). I also use it just to encourage myself to better myself in general (ex: days since I’ve skipped exercising, days since I’ve had an argument/confrontation with someone). Love seeing the amount of years/months/days/hours go up little by little until the number is huger than I ever thought possible— very rewarding feeling! In areas of life I practice temperance/moderation instead of abstinence and in areas of life I’m just trying to better myself it’s still encouraging to see my “longest steak” & “average streak” increase slowly overtime—it prevents me from feeling guilty or ashamed when I “lapse” and have to reset the counter because I focus on my streak instead of the fact that I lapsed/failed. Sometimes I feel a tiny but noticeable amount of disappointment and/or frustration when i lapse and have to reset the counter (no guilt or shame though so it’s fine) but I think that’s normal because it just remotivates me to discipline myself more so I can improve my steak in the future. Very good for learning self discipline and holding yourself accountable for your actions. Highly recommend if you have a personality like mine!

Only features I would like to have: 1)More decorative colors for the counters. I wish all of mine could be different. 2) An option to display the way your streak is displayed when you tap on “year”. For example my counter for “Red Meat” shows as “3 years | 8 months | 16 days | 16 hours” because of the way I’m naturally inclined to count time in my head I wish I had the option to display it as “3 years | 8 months | 2 weeks | 2.5 days”

I definitely recommend to anyone trying to quit a bad habit!

title: extremely helpful app!
body:
since i started using this app i’ve noticed how much improvement i’ve made. i know a lot of people say not to track things since it seems to hyper-fixate your mind on your habits/addictions, but this the way that i see it:

once you spend time and effort into doing (or in this sense, not doing) something and see the progress of how long you’ve been doing that for, it makes you value your effort more.

think of it like a snapchat streak. nobody really cares about what snaps you send anymore after the first few weeks, but what matters is the time and energy you’ve invested into doing something for so long that in your brain you grow to care for it and wouldn’t do anything to ruin it. it’s a motivation.

since i started using this app i’d constantly be attentive every day of how many hours i’d gone without indulging in bad habits, but slowly it slipped my mind. i stopped checking the days and even thinking about it in the first place. yes i had cravings but looking at that effort i put in made me see the clear picture. every now and then i check it just to give myself a confidence boost, or a mental reward i should say. i highly, HIGHLY recommend this app to anyone who has trouble detaching from habits.

title: Simple, Aesthetic, and Functional!
body: It's exactly what I was looking for! A simple way to track my streaks. I love this, since it makes it so much easier for me to quit things when I can *visually* see with my eyes I've been clean for weeks or months and I realize just how far I've come. This app couldn't have made it easier. It's extremely simple, you just create a streak with the “+” button and reset it with a button when you relapse. I bet your GRANDMA could use this app to overcome her crippling crack cocaine addiction! On top of this, it's aesthetically a very pretty app. I love the minimalistic approach the creators took, just like you'd expect for such a simple and easy to use app like this. Most importantly out of everything though, this app does it's job flawlessly. I haven't encountered a single issue yet! It's got widget implementation, a very fairly and cheaply priced premium version (which isn't anywhere near necessary to have in order to use the app), and finally a very nice locking feature (via face ID or passcode) so no one but you can access the app if you need to keep people out. Also many more features, those are just my favorites. FR though, what are you doing? Download this app already and see for yourself! I love this app, thank you! :D

title: I do love this app. 5-stars for one additional feature
body: I do love this app. Especially the ability to reset a streak. This creates a nice history log. For example, if you quit smoking for 5 days, had a cigarette, then reset, over time you can see the history of streaks/attempts. The one thing that would make this really nice is when upon resetting a streak, you could have the ability to “pause”, so another streak wouldn’t automatically start. Taking the smoking example, if a person quit smoking for 20 days, then started smoking and didn’t quit again until 10 days later, they could reset their streak, when they started to smoke, pause the streak, and then when they try quitting again, in this case 10 days later, they could start the streak up again. Other than that, I really like this app. To have that additional feature would just turn it from a 4-star review to a 5- star review. And it doesn’t seem like it would be that hard to implement so get on it!!! :-)

body: I have been using this app for months and it is an incredibly helpful tool when it comes to remembering and keeping track of the time passed since whatever it is you’re counting days since. I use this app as a way to keep track of when I last had symptoms related to my Mental Health diagnoses- Depression, Anxiety, BPD, PTSD - and it is so helpful. This app is similar to a “set it and forget it” approach where you enter the date and time and after that initial save it is all kept in the app. I have mine set so it’s not a recurring reminder of “it’s been this many days since X” and is more of an app that I open to check my progress and document any relapses. Great app and much of the app is available for use without purchasing anything.

title: I love this app because time is elusive.
body: I use this app to track all the new things I try. It’s so simple to use and just sits there and keeps track of how much time is going by. I used to ask myself, “When did I start doing that?” And try to figure it out, never knowing if I was right. Now I record the start date in Days Since, and open it up when I’m wondering and can see how long I’ve been working on each goal. I love that I can use fun bright colors to make the time tracking cards and I love that I can reset my counters when needed. I also love that it counts seconds, minutes, hours, and days. I’ve been using it for three months. It’s pretty nifty.

title: Exactly What I Need
body: Been using Days Since for almost a month now and have found it incredibly helpful in tracking and cutting down my alcohol, caffeine, and cannabis use. I love the ability to take down a note of my feelings or the circumstances whenever I reset my counter. Looking at my failures as “data points” has been very useful for both my mental health and overall progress in my goals. Amazing app, great job from the Days Since team :)

title: Appreciate it, would like to suggest more.
body: I’m satisfied with the simplicity of this app. I’m currently using it for a sobriety counter, and would like to suggest some features that could potentially be helpful. I also understand if these suggestions are not the direction you’re going for, as I can tell by the design it’s more to be used as a simple counter/tool. Anyway, the first suggestion I had was any sort of notification-specific rewards or reminders. Something like “your ___ counter has reached ___ days, congrats!” And maybe having an option to select from a negative, neutral, or positive message or set to none/no notifications. These can be counter specific as well. (Hypothetically). My next suggestion was a “stop counting” option, like if you no longer want to count it after a certain amount of days, and then maybe a notification that was like “your ____ counter stopped, check it out!” (I don’t know) Or a way to make it so that certain lack of use doesn’t count towards your overall progress statistics—sometimes I forget to track or have something else going on that day and don’t want my lack of counting to affect the statistics of the progress I’ve made. I can probably think of more but at the moment I’m stumped and should be getting some sleep. So goodnight and thank you for this great app.

title: Days since is great!!!
body: This app is truly amazing. It's unbelievable how much easier this makes it to harness my willpower for my own personal growth. I am not giving a full five stars however because I see some fairly simple ways in which this app's effectiveness could be even further increased. There should be a "points system" where you can see your "current days since score", which is the number of days of all of your current active streaks added up. If this were combined with a simple points over time line graph visualization, users would be further incentivized to continue their streaks. Additionally, you could add in simple "sticker" type graphical award incentives (like snapchat streak emojis) to further increase the apps effectiveness. Keep up the great work and please implement these things!!

title: Really Amazing App!!!
body: I’ve had a few bad habits that I have managed to quit using this app. I’ve said goodbye to junk food, too much inactivity, and smoking. I’ve also been spending significantly less time on my phone these days. Now I just say, like probably many people, I had reached a crossroads. So as to say, once I dropped all my bad habits successfully, it felt as if there was nothing special about it other than knowing I’m on a road to better health. For anyone who may be struggling with that, there’s a few things I’ve learned and gained in addition from just reflecting on myself and my past bad habits. Removing bad habits (addictions) allows you to live in the present moment. Admittedly, this was very scary at first. You become highly aware of your own mortality. I have learned to embrace it though and I am working on building productive habits to replace the bad habits. So my advice to you is to work on replacing the bad habits with healthy and productive habits. Because if not then you will be left with a void. You’re going to feel this emptiness. This sense of losing purpose. Keep in mind that bad habits you used to do constantly kept your mind distracted and running from traumas and such. It’s a good opportunity to face all of your traumas head on and let go of everything bad. It will be easier than you think. Don’t question the process. Just trust it.

title: This One
body:
Simple and easy to use interface, understated graphics, robust reliability, and (a rarity these days) as good as it gets privacy protection!!!  Always investigate that for any app.  After trying other apps, this is the one I’m keeping.  (re: Version 1.16.8 June, 2022)

I'm using this as a general purpose days-since counter (rather than for behavior modification… although I probably should!) and for general use I have 3 suggestions:

1)It would be more accommodating of a larger number of entries (and possibly users) by allowing an option to display counters in single, stacked, horizontal lines for less scrolling.  But as is works great to emphasize the importance and separateness of each entry.

2)It might be helpful to also have options to automatically sort entries by most days since, and to reverse that sort.

3)Add the ability to group sub entries under a common subject.

Nice work!

title: Very Useful, But Better With a Few Tweaks:
body:
This app is great. It tracks your progress and doesn’t judge you for resetting a counter should you give in to whatever reason you set it for. The calendar view is a great tangible way to see how you do throughout each month, and I even use it to keep accountability with a friend so they can keep tabs on my own progress. Tracking how long on average you go before a reset and what your longest period between resets was is also a great way to judge your progress and mark your own milestones. For any of you looking to try a nice and simple solution to break some bad habits, give this one a shot. It’s free, and is very intuitive to use, granted that you keep up with your own progress and document each time you need to reset a counter. 

One thing I’d really like though is this: you already allow the removal of resets if you tap the edit button when searching through resets on a given counter. It would be awesome if you were able to edit the comment or time there as well, just so you wouldn’t have to delete and redo the reset if you realize you forgot to document something or put AM instead of PM or something like that. Other than that, I really can’t complain, but that tiny missing feature has bugged me for a while, so I thought I’d write a review and mention it. Other than that, this app is extremely simple and could use a bit of polish here and there. Things like milestone markers for longest streak on the calendar itself could be large incentives for lasting longer without a reset. Perhaps even milestones for increasing the average time between resets could encourage further control over bad habits. Just a few ideas for the future if you are so inclined. ;) Thanks for reading!

title: Keeps me on track
body: I like this App. I can set more than one category and when I open the app the info is all on one page. For me it’s motivating to look at how long I’ve been working towards a goal.  I set two goals for myself 1)Days without refined sugar and 2) Days without alcoholic beverages. Neither of these goals was set out of a critical need but more of a personal desire to achieve better overall health. Last night we had a dinner party and we were serving cocktails and I briefly thought, I’ll just have one drink with everyone else, but I opened the app and saw that it had been 16 days since I last had a beverage and I really didn’t want to hit restart on that counter! So I passed on the beverages and woke up feeling great today and proud that I stuck with my decision to continue on a healthy path. However, I did eat a couple of Oreos and had to reset my refined sugar counter to 0. This is a great tool to track progress and can be a great motivator for people who like to set personal goals.

title: A fairly good app
body: There’s nothing special about this app. This app was alright, though. All that it really does is allows you to set a habit tracker and you make sure that you don’t do it again. I have three bad habits that I need to break, but again this app is pretty normal and it helps to remind me that I need to quit. It also helps with being able to see how many days I’ve gone without doing it again because it encourages and motivates me to keep going. Although, once I really do quit my habit what else is there to do? There is no flair or anything super special they happens if I did hit a one year milestone. I like that you can reset the counter, but I want to know, developer, where is the pizzazz that I’m looking for or a little something to keep me motivated. What if those numbers aren’t enough? This is what I would like to see as an improvement to this app. Push notifications. With these enabled, you can see motivating quotes or a little sentence to remind you that you’re doing a great job. I feel that this can also be done in the app itself so that you can also view inspiring reminders if you keep visiting the app to see your progress. I know that there can be many more visual pleasing updates that can be added to this app but definitely keep my advice in mind. Thank you for your time.

Changing a habit is challenging.The tools you use to track progress shouldn’t be.  I love how easy it was to get started with this app and customize it to track my specific goals.  It took less than 5 minutes from download to set up and best of all, it’s free! No gimmicks, no sneaky sales techniques- just immediate, easy to use, customizable tracking.

This app immediately met my needs and the results speak for themselves.  I am now 97 days into a habit change I’ve been struggling with for 5 years and 63 days into another. Thank you for contributing to my success!

title: Awareness to the max
body:
This app has helped me to be aware of my good and bad habits and be accountable for myself. Something humbling comes to mind when I need to reset my clock when falling into a bad habit. And a bit of pride when I see the clock going up in hours when working in a good habit. 
If you are looking for a way to keep you accountable for your habits, this might be a good options. At least it was for me, as I am always using my phone during the day. It is easy for me to see that  widget every time I open my main screen. Whether you are improving a habit such as working out, meditation or breaking a vice such as stop smoking, or falling from my diet, this app can help you as long as you are open to be honest to yourself.

title: Clean, no nonsense app
body:
Ever since I’ve switched over from android I’ve noticed that free apps always seem to have a catch on iOS. This is probably the first app where I feel like the developers truly wanted to make an app that could help people with out other intentions like ad revenue and marketing. It is a breath of fresh air to use something that is both free and useful. 
Overall this app does what it says it does, it tracks habits, promotes quitting and helps keep everything in perspective. This app is stupidly clean and simple, exactly what the developers were intending. The ui is intuitive and discovery is simple. Each button and element reacts how I think it should and the widgets are well done and straightforward. Thats about all of the synonyms I have for “cleanly done”. Good job guys.

title: Very helpful.
body: I’ve been on the mission to stop smoking for some time now. I always thought it would be impossible because for me I get that urge to smoke when I don’t have it. This was always why I’m past times I would say “I could never stop” but by the Grace of My Lord and Savior Jesus I’ve been able to overcome so much more than I thought I would. I got a Bible and started reading and when I would read the Bible on those days I wouldn’t have as many urges. Crazy to think that reading a book could feminism physical addiction urges right? The app was a great way for me to keep track of my progress to remind myself if I ever do get an urge or an apatite for smoking. I still do get urges occasionally if I havnt been reading my Bible but that’s why I love the app so much. It gives me motivation and it gives me something to physically see. If you do mess up there’s no shame because you can reset that timer and your back at it again. You can make different timers for different things too maybe you vape also or maybe you smoke weed or something. You can set different timers for all the things you need to tackle no matter what it is so I think the app is great and I’m really appreciative of it!

title: Great Motivation for Both Healthy/Unhealthy Habits
body:
This app is so helpful of keeping track of how long I’ve made it since I’ve kicked some nasty habits (vaping, binge eating, and consuming alcohol). It’s so motivating to see how far I’ve come, and when I’m thinking of relapse, just looking at this counter makes me not want to break my streak. 

You can also use it for positive reminders, like days since you had a baby or a new pet, so you can celebrate those mini milestones. Or days since you’ve picked up a healthy habit, like eating a balanced diet, started a fitness routine, started a new job, the possibilities are endless. 

Overall, a great app. The only thing I would like to see in the future is possibly allowing reminders to check in. Not every day, but I’ll admit, once or twice I should have reset my counter and forgot. It’s a problem with myself though, and perhaps others prefer to not receive notifications.

title: Maybe it’s simple enough to work?
body:
I gave it three stars because I don’t like that the only way to really hold yourself accountable is to post it on social media (they gave that as an option in the app). I would prefer other features, A different kind of reward system. Or even just a simple reminder to look at my progress throughout the day or the week or whatever. Right now it’s pretty cool but I’m worried I’m going to forget about the app and it’s going to get lost in my homepage. Other than that, I think basic premise is pretty cool. It just needs some really simple additions, like a notification system 

edit: I updated my review from three stars to four. It’s actually working better than I thought it would. I still wish there was some type of notification or reminder to check it. Very simple counter system without a lot of bells and whistles. I am six days into no smoking . If I make it to 30, I’ll update it to five stars

title: Help me break a bad habit fast
body:
I was trying to stop drinking alcohol and I struggled to stay consistent. This app has been the best tool yet. Even better than the other apps aimed at breaking addiction. It is a simple tool that makes you feel like you make progress fast. I like how you can track in hours, days, weeks, etc. I moved from hours to days and then to weeks as time went on and it gave me a fresh look. The only things I would add to the app is the ability to edit the date. I found this app a few days into my fast and I wish I could edit the date to reflect the actual start date instead of the date I found the app. I just had to always add 3 days to the app’s date. Note to developers!! 

Thanks for this tool!! It is great!

title: Best AD-FREE counter app out there!
body:
Let me just start off by saying, I really adore this app! It’s so functional, simple, and aesthetically clean. It’s great to see an app that’s actually designed for its practicality and for its users! If you are looking for a app to count how many days it’s been, all the way down to the second, this is the perfect app! I really cannot recommend it enough!

Pros
NO ADS! (Astonishing, I know)
Simple to use
Great design
Very clear interface

And for the developers I have only one small complaint about the app, the lack of color choices for the counters. If it were at all possible (I don’t know how difficult coding is) I believe that adding a color wheel to the color options would be a great feature. Having only 15 color choices does make things very simple, but also limits users. Of course it’s not the end of the world if that’s not doable but that is the only complaint I have! Thank you for the small indie team that makes this wonderful app that helps tons of people :)

I set goals and “days since” for my nicotine habit, when my last meal eating out was, when I had unhealthy food last, and even for going over on screen time limitations I set up for myself on my phone. It’s kept me accountable in so many ways, and now after using this app and having the courage to push forward I’m nicotine free, workout daily and eat healthy, and have lessened my gaming extensively. I can tell you from the other side, whatever you’re thinking about using this for, do it.

title: Trackable self-accountability
body:
I’ve been using this app to try and focus on daily habits that I’m usually not very good at. I use it to make sure that I’ve taken care of myself in a way that’s difficult for a sprint of days, and the fact that it tracks resets is a gentle encouragement and a useful type of accountability.

I keep a useful widget on my home screen that shows how many days it’s been since I’ve had alcohol, and how many days it’s been since I made another large change in my life that has been positive. It’s minimal and non-intrusive and not pushy. No reminders that shame you if you’ve had to reset no notifications to tell you that you need to check it, it’s incredibly passive if you don’t deal well with pressure. It just reminds you how long you’ve been doing a thing and how many times you’ve failed at sticking to that routine. That little bit of accountability has really changed my perspective

This has become a vital part of my self-care routine and I really really appreciate how simple and useful this app is.

title: Works Perfect For My Needs
body: App is free and does everything I need it to do. Actually it does a little more than I need as well because it also keeps track of things other than just how many hours/days/weeks/months/years (and yes you can easily switch between those time units to see how long it’s been) but also see things like your longest time without, your average time without, and how long you’ve been keeping such a counter. It’s also nice that it lets you rename your counters whatever you’d like. I’d rather not have the direct words for what I’m keeping track of on the counter, so I often write abbreviations and I know what it means. You can also change the colors of the counters and thats fun. Ive had this app for a little over a year and I’d definitely recommend it to anyone needing to keep track of days since, for which the app is named promptly. I’m probably forgetting some other features just because I’ve had it so long and Im used to them, but absolutely its a wonderful app. I’ve also never encountered an ad, or needed to pay for something to unlock special features, which is really nice considering that when I have to reset my counters I’m not in a good mental state so having to wait for ads and be bombarded by other content would be overwhelming and frustrating. Honestly I’ve never encountered anything on it that I think would need fixing, as “too good to be true” as that sounds, it really is just an app made incredibly well. Overall an excellent app that does everything I need and more; it’s designed really well both in terms of function and aesthetic. Easily navigated and takes next to no time to learn how to use. Would 100% recommend to anyone looking to keep track of days since any habit.

title: Extremely Helpful
body: Days Since is an excellent app, and I’m more than delighted to have found it. Prior to finding Days Since, I used standard counters. Many varieties of them. I tried them for months at a time, but didn’t get the same result I was looking for. I’ve used Days Since to assist me in quitting smoking as well as other vices I’m a bit too embarrassed to reveal here. I’ve used it to help me keep up with water intake, keep up with speaking to specific family members, as well as progression in working on various projects. For each instance, Days Since has effectively revealed to me…..well, ME. It has shown me just how much of a procrastinator I can be, or just how amazingly consistent I can be. I love this app, and have recommended it to numerous friends who could use a bit of insight into how they are realistically managing their lives. Thank you, Days Since Team. You clearly “get” people like me, for whom striving to be better is a daily endeavor. The days since I found Days Since are much better than they were before.  Thank you again!

What’s also nice about the app’s format is that it makes it possible to also track GOOD habits. I sometimes struggle remembering to take my medication, so I made a counter that can tell me how much time has gone by since I last took it. 

For good habits that might not be daily such as exercising, the “average streak” part of the counter provides some insight on how often I go without doing a certain habit and even gives some motivation to do it more often.

title: A review and suggestion. Good for people struggling with mental illnesses, but could be even better!
body:
Hi. This is going to get a little bit deep, so here’s a warning to anyone reading this: TW for anxiety, depression, panic attack, and s*lf-h*rm mentions.
~—~—~—~
Mental health usage: I’ve been using this app for a while now, since late September 2020, and it gets my stamp of approval. As well as using it to track more lighthearted and nice things like how long I’ve been with my partner (126 days as of posting this review! 💖), I also use it to track things relating to my mental health. I have anxiety and depression, which makes my life really hard. I have therefore made counters on this app for things like how long it’s been since I’ve had a panic attack, or how long it’s been since I’ve had a thought about s*lf-h*rm. Opening this app and seeing those numbers stack up: “No S*lf-H*rm Thoughts: 10 days.” “30 days.” “50 days.” That really just makes me so proud of myself, and makes me feel so much better than anything else ever has. No amount of therapists trying to cheer me on or nice internet posts can make me feel as proud of myself for getting through another day without having a panic attack or thinking about s*lf-h*rming as opening up this app and looking at that little counter. 

General appreciation: I appreciate how it’s not all up in my face, instead just a nice little background motivator, because my ADHD and anxiety make me super overwhelmed when I’m being pressured to do something. When I’m being pressured to do something, I eventually get so overwhelmed that I don’t end up doing it at all, and I’m so glad that that’s not the case with this app!
It’s so nice how you can color-customize each counter, and set whether you want it to show days, weeks, etc.. I also love how the developers clearly take the time to look at and read reviews, and implement the suggestions left for them. I especially love that as I was reading through the reviews to see if my suggestion was already asked by someone else, I could see that the developers had replied on reviews of people being happy about making progress to congratulate them, that’s so sweet and kind!

Suggestion: The only reason this wonderful app gets a four-star review is the lack of a feature that could take this over the top: a toggleable counter, like a switch. This was something I was disappointed to find doesn’t exist currently. For example, I suffer from long periods of mutism, where I physically cannot make myself talk. It would be super nice to have a counter with a switch, so I could mark how long it’s been since I’ve spoken or how long it’s been since I’ve gone through a period of mutism - its natural state would be “Days since I’ve had a period of mutism”, and when I’m mute, I can toggle that switch to the other side, “Days since I’ve spoken”, which would count how long it’s been since I toggled the switch to that side. Then when I’m speaking again, I’d toggle it again, and it would start counting how long it’s been since my last period of mutism again - like merging two counters into one. I hope this makes sense, and I hope it’s something that can be implemented in the future! :D
Another quick suggestion that wasn’t important enough to affect my star rating - I’d like to see a fully custom color wheel color picker. I do appreciate how lovely the in-app palette of colors looks, but it would be nice to have the option of both the palette and the free choice. However, again, this isn’t that important.
If one or both of these features could be added, this would be amazing and definitely bump up my review to 5 stars! Thank you so much, developer team, for being so considerate and friendly, and for working so hard to bring us this amazing free app.

Thanks,
- Arsyn (please disregard whatever account name shows at the top, if you don’t mind ^^’)

title: Works really well!
body:
I have been using this app to track my days since for about 3 months.
It tracks also the hours minutes and seconds, which is very cool.
It is a able to track multiple timers at once.
If you slip and need to reset, it tracks your number of resets and longest streak. It has a calendar that shows your streaks to track progress.
It gives a lot of encouragement to open the app and see my days since.
My initial concern was that the app might crash and lose progress. But over 3 months it has never crashed.
Past 26 days I have only slipped 1 day!
Great app
